title: Rodrigo González de Puebla (London) to Miguel Pérez de Almazán, 21 Apr 1506, in Puebla's First Cipher, AGS Patronato Real leg. 54 doc. 78 (catalogue 617)

documents.shelfmark: AGS, Patronato Real, leg. 54, doc. 78 (PARES description 2208120; foliation 179)
documents.route: De Puebla (London) -> Miguel Pérez de Almazán (Castile)

plaintext.source: No interlinear or separate decipherment; none found in CSP Spain I, the 1868 Supplement or Fuensalida's Correspondencia (1907).

transcription.source: PARES show/2208120, image 1 (1017 x 1413 px), 3x crops
transcription.notes: 373 cipher signs and code groups (counted from transcription.txt, clear text excluded). Corrections in the second pass: l. 16 crossed L + o (quien), l. 19 single C, l. 29 'va a' added. ll. 11-13 not re-read.

system.summary: Puebla's First Cipher: a letter substitution with homophones for a, b/v, c, e, i (Tomokiyo's reconstruction of Bergenroth's key no. 6), with one Great Roman Numeral code group (DCCCLXXXVIII, el Rey de Inglaterra); cipher passages set inside clear text.
system.sibling_key: Same First Cipher as targets/puebla1507 (15 Apr 1507, printed in the 1868 Supplement); the code group from the key of targets/puebla1495 and puebla1496 (AGS PTR leg. 52 doc. 33).
system.notes: Sign o serves u and v. One sign (l. 13, in 'ra?on') is not in Tomokiyo's table; a Z with a hook gives z [?].

prior_solution.where: None found in CSP Spain I (April 1506, pp. 385-386), the 1868 Supplement (1506), Fuensalida's Correspondencia (1907), CODOIN vol. 8 (1846), Paz y Meliá's Series de los más importantes documentos ... Medinaceli vols. 1-2 (1915-22), Rodríguez Villa's Juana la Loca (1892), Mattingly EHR 1940, or an Internet Archive full-text search for the reading's phrases (27 Oct 2026). Tomokiyo lists the letter without a reading; the source of his page carries an HTML comment with the first words of l. 11 ('y dela parti da ....'), so he had begun to decipher it. HathiTrust, Google Books, BNE Hispánica and Mattingly's Catherine of Aragon (1941) not searched in full text. A parallel independent reading by Brice Dudout, with the same Tomokiyo table, was published the same day (Europe chiffrée, 27 Oct 2026); it credits two readings taken from this one.

conditions.human_role: WAINUT: the owner set the task (catalogue items 615-617). The work was done by AI language-model agents, and a second agent re-read the cipher on fresh crops with its own decoder. No human reading.

solution.what: PARES show/2208120: 4 images; watermark PTR,LEG,54,78; address to Almazán and endorsement 'del doctor de la puebla ... xxj ... abril 1506' on image 4.
Cipher passages of image 1, ll. 11-29, transcribed in ASCII aliases from 3x crops (transcription.txt).

Tomokiyo's First Cipher table applied: 'por su propio interese que la princesa me escriviese estas cartas que aqui van inclusas', 'los de la señora princesa veo tan bien ataviados que mas no pense ver', 'codicia de algunas personas', 'tesoro de [?el Rey de Inglaterra]'.
Word-list cover of the decode: key 0.608; 1000 shuffled keys max 0.292; key on 1000 shuffled texts max 0.262 (decode.py). Alphabet shifts of 1-3 give gibberish.
Second agent re-read ll. 14-20, 24-26 and 29 in its own alias set and decoder: all readings reproduced; corrections at l. 16 (quien), l. 19 (single C), l. 29 (va a).
CSP Spain I April 1506 (BHO, fetched again: nos. 458-460, no Puebla letter); 1868 Supplement 1506; Fuensalida 1907 OCR searched for the distinctive phrases: no earlier reading.

Maintainer review (Claude for Daniel Bourdeau): key_first_cipher.tsv checked sign by sign against Tomokiyo's table image Puebla1.jpg (cryptiana): every value agrees (a = q/M, b/v = o/p, c = Pi, d = long s, e = +, f = g, g = f, h = a, i/y = b/5, l = e, m = lambda, n = alpha, o = z-forms, p = U, q = crossed L, r = 46, s = barred T, t = R, u = o); the table has no z.

Shared language model es-golden-age (order 5, no spaces) on the decoded runs of ll. 14-29: key -1.692 per letter; 1000 shuffled keys best -4.734 (median -6.117); key on 1000 sign-shuffled texts best -4.258 (median -4.773). lm.best_language on the word-divided reading: es-modern -1.617 first, ca-modern -1.946, pt-modern -2.093 (decode.py).

Print search for this letter: OCR of CODOIN vol. 8, Paz y Meliá Series vols. 1-2, Rodríguez Villa 1892, Crónica del rey Enrico Otavo 1874 appendix, Mattingly EHR 55 (1940) grepped for the reading's distinctive words and for Puebla letters of April 1506; Internet Archive full-text search for seven phrases: no earlier text. Found a commented-out note 'y dela parti da ....' in the source of Tomokiyo's Spanish-ciphers page beside this letter. HathiTrust full-text search blocked by a Cloudflare challenge (not bypassed).

Reading reviewed as sentences; l. 29 'va a beneficio de natura' identified as the period phrase 'left to nature / to chance' (Cisneros's secretaries 1516, CODOIN) and retranslated; two translation sentences smoothed. No change to the decryption.

Maintainer review tried to fetch image 1 of show/2208120 for the cipher snip and a re-read of the unread signs (l. 13, l. 25): PARES answered HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests) to every request, site-wide, from about 11:45 to 13:10; nothing opened.

Brice Dudout's parallel, independent reading published (https://bdudout.github.io/europe-chiffree/en/documents.html#puebla-1506): same table frozen, 363 of 366 signs; the decipherments agree word for word on S01, S02, S06-S08, S10-S11, S13, S15, S16; he adopts "a beneficio de natura" and "por aquella gente hazia" from this one. He reads z in "ra?on" (l. 13), "de la" (S05), "pedrique" (l. 16), and transcribes the clear text of ll. 11-17; not checked here (PARES 429).

texts.label: ll. 18-29: the passages that read
texts.summary: De Puebla tells Almazán that people around the Princess of Wales, for their own interest, had her write the letters he encloses; that he sees her household finely dressed beyond expectation; and that the greed of certain persons is such that he doubts even the treasure of [?the King of England] would content them. Written as Philip and Juana were about to sail from England; Katharine's own letter of the next day (CSP I no. 459) says her people were all but naked.

reading_review.note: Read reading.txt against decryption.txt as sentences. 'por su propio interese que la princesa me escriviese estas cartas que aqui van inclusas' and 'los de la señora princesa veo tan bien ataviados que mas no pense ver' are whole, idiomatic sentences; 'la codicia de algunas personas [?] [?] es tal que con el tesoro de [el Rey de Inglaterra] dudo que se contentasen' is coherent with two unread signs and a doubtful code word; l. 29 is a fragment ('va a beneficio de natura', a set phrase, retranslated). Every passage is cut at both ends by unread clear text, so the reading is coherent but raw: grade B, not A.

texts.label: ll. 11-17: fragments
texts.note: Secure words (y de la partida; senora princesa; conviene; bien y acrecentamiento; de [?el Rey de Inglaterra] y del principe; abra quien le [?pedir] que ningun malcontentamiento), but the clear words between them are not read, so no sentences.

texts.label: Puebla to Almazán, 21 April 1506: parallel reading by Brice Dudout
texts.summary: An autograph letter from the Catholic Monarchs’ ambassador in England to Ferdinand the Catholic’s secretary, written on the eve of the departure of Philip the Handsome and Juana, who had been driven onto the English coast three months earlier. Sixteen cipher passages, never read until now, defend the household of Catherine of Aragon.

reading_review.note: The cipher passages ([[...]]) read as coherent Spanish sentences and agree with the reading in reading.txt; the clear text between them is given only where certain, so most sentences carry [...] for clear words not established, which is why the checker scores 38%. The translation follows the same marks.
